look_here_first: Inspect an opposite leaf pair on an unpruned shoot: blades are thin, usually 1–3 inches long, often hairy beneath along the midvein, with hairy petioles and young stems. Confirm short terminal and upper-axillary white flower panicles.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Native to eastern Asia; introduced in North America. Learner-approved encounter/comparison taxon, not a confirmed target-zone native.

morphology_keys.habit: Evergreen to semi-evergreen, many-stemmed shrub often forming dense thickets by suckering.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite, simple, entire, elliptic to oblong, usually 1–3 inches long, thinner than L. lucidum; hairs along underside midvein and on petioles.
morphology_keys.flowers: Small white four-lobed flowers in shorter terminal or upper-axillary panicles, usually about 2–3 inches long.
morphology_keys.fruit: Clusters of purple-black to black drupes.
morphology_keys.stems: Young twigs often hairy, with lenticels; can form suckering thickets.

comparisons.key_distinctions: L. lucidum typically has larger 3–6 inch glossy leathery leaves with an opaque marginal rim and 6–8 sunken lateral veins, and larger terminal panicles. Ilex vomitoria (native yaupon) has alternate, often crenate leaves, not opposite entire leaves; check nodes rather than leaf color.
comparisons.cautions: Privets vary with pruning, shade, and juvenile growth. Use multiple mature leaves, nodes, venation and panicle structure; do not use fruit color alone.

diagnostic_image_needs: Matched mature leaf top and underside with scale
Leaf margin, midvein hair and petiole macro
